verses.english: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Tassa kāye kāyānupassino viharato yo kāyasmiṁ chando so pahīyati.
verses.english: As they do so they give up desire for the body.
When desire is given up they realize freedom from death.

verses.pali: Vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Tassa vedanāsu vedanānupassino viharato yo vedanāsu chando so pahīyati.
verses.english: As they do so they give up desire for feelings.
When desire is given up they realize freedom from death.

verses.pali: Citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Tassa citte cittānupassino viharato yo cittamhi chando so pahīyati.
verses.english: As they do so they give up desire for the mind.
When desire is given up they realize freedom from death.

verses.pali: Dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Tassa dhammesu dhammānupassino viharato yo dhammesu chando so pahīyati.
verses.english: As they do so they give up desire for principles.
When desire is given up they realize freedom from death.”
